name: Kengoro
summary: The successor to Kenshiro from the University of Tokyo's JSK lab: a tendon-driven musculoskeletal humanoid with 108 motors and a porous metal skeleton that 'sweats' water to cool itself, letting it hold demanding poses like push-ups. It is used to study human-like whole-body motion and internal body systems.
notable: Can do sit-ups and push-ups under musculoskeletal control
